clue.text: Smug personality paid in full

blocks.note: your self is your individual personality
a debt or creditor is satisfied when paid off completely

explanation.surface: Someone pleased with themselves after a large fee has been settled in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased with oneself to an irritating degree is exactly what a smug person shows, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Crack charwoman's first predilection - housework

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the cleaner's title

blocks.note: to spring is to split or crack, as timber or a mast does
the first letter of charwoman
a leaning is an inclination or preference

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's top priority being a thorough round of housework.
explanation.walkthrough: A charwoman is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-cleaning is the thorough annual cleaning of a home, so it is a particular round of domestic chores.

clue.text: Clear headed Law Lord covering Channel Islands

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the judge's title goes outside the islands

blocks.note: Lud is a lord, as in a barrister's 'm'lud' to the judge
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A sharp-minded senior judge whose jurisdiction extends to Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are Jersey, Guernsey and their neighbours off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid describes someone thinking rationally and clearly, so it is a synonym of having a clear, sane mind.

clue.text: One who deceives a police officer? Splendid!

blocks.note: super is short for a police superintendent
a duper is a person who tricks others

explanation.surface: A con artist fooling a senior policeman, greeted with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: One who deceives a super is a super-duper, so the phrase reads as its own compound with the officer first.
explanation.definitionFit: Super-duper is jokey informal slang for something marvellous or excellent, so it means splendid.

clue.text: They take things wrongly, being reputedly thick

blocks.note: first meaning: people who steal
second meaning: the saying 'thick as ...', for close friends

explanation.surface: People who misunderstand things and are said to be stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take things wrongly' looks like misunderstanding, and 'thick' like stupid; both are steals and the idiom for intimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are people who steal property, and the proverb says close companions are as thick, or intimate, as they are.

clue.text: Farewell party to enrapture a cricket side

blocks.note: to send someone is to thrill them
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A leaving do laid on to delight a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces, the other being the on or leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off is a gathering held to say goodbye to someone departing, so it is a celebration of leave-taking.

clue.text: Second judge initially withdraws, being uncertain

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
withdrawing means leaving, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a jiffy is a moment, as in 'just a second'
the first letter of judge

explanation.surface: A second judge pulls out of a case because they are unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number; it is a short moment, JIFFY, which loses its J.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious, full of ifs, so it means uncertain or questionable.

clue.text: Belief about exploit engenders expectation of failure

indicators.note: about means around, so the belief wraps the exploit

blocks.note: deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene
an exploit is a bold deed, a feat

explanation.surface: Doubts about some daring venture breed a gloomy sense that it will all go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the attitude of anticipating or accepting loss too readily, so it is a pessimistic outlook expecting to lose.

clue.text: Short break for soldiers in swimming area

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the swimming area

blocks.note: a place for bathing, or swimming
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops on brief leave at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: RE goes after the B of BATHING: B-RE-ATHING SPACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a brief pause to rest or recover before carrying on, so it is a short respite.

clue.text: Quality of radio signal in part of hotel

blocks.note: first meaning: how well a broadcast is picked up, good or poor
second meaning: the front desk where guests check in

explanation.surface: A guest complaining that the radio only gets a decent signal in one corner of the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both how clearly a set picks up broadcasts and the hotel desk area where arriving guests are greeted.

clue.text: Player's condition accepted by retiring judge

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the judge word is read in the opposite direction
being accepted by something means being taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a ref (referee) judges a game
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A musician's terms being agreed to by a judge who is about to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'retiring' looks like a shy judge but means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifer plays the fife, a small shrill flute heard in military bands, so this is a kind of musical performer.

clue.text: In tribulation, a director's lowest point

indicators.note: the answer is said to be in the following words, sitting inside them across the word break

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of tribulation through a into the start of director

explanation.surface: A film director hitting rock bottom during a time of great hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom of anything, originally the point of the sky directly below the observer, so the lowest point.

clue.text: Small part of book about island's old music-maker

indicators.note: about means going around, so the book part wraps the island

blocks.note: a volume is part of a multi-volume book, and small means abbreviated to VOL
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A short passage in a book about an island's ancient musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol is a bowed stringed instrument of the Renaissance, a forerunner of the violin family, so an old instrument.

clue.text: Artistic movement Democrat's First Lady joined

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
Ada is a woman's name; the setter treats it as the original lady, perhaps Adah, the first named wife in Genesis after Eve

explanation.surface: A US president's wife, a Democrat's First Lady, signing up to an avant-garde art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like the president's wife; here it is just a lady's name, ADA, after D for Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was the anti-art movement founded in Zurich around 1916, so it is an example of an artistic school.

clue.text: Player's adaptation of French tale

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks the original, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor's version of a story from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests an actor in a stage adaptation; it is a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre-half is a central defender in football, a position on the team, so the answer is a kind of footballer.

clue.text: Flag officer -not the enemy's

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
what is not theirs is ours

explanation.surface: A naval flag officer insisting a flag belongs to our side, not the enemy's.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its flag, so the plural noun is a standard synonym for a banner or ensign.

clue.text: Organisation formed to record one's nervous spasms

blocks.note: a log is a written record
one is I, so one's is I'S
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A society set up so members can note their nervous twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Logistics is the planning and coordination of supplies, people and transport, so it is the work of organising an operation.

clue.text: Language of European maiden - one appearing in person?

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the person, so they are placed within that word

blocks.note: in person means in the flesh
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman from Europe asking whether somebody is turning up in person.
explanation.walkthrough: FLESH takes M and I inside: FLE-M-I-SH. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish is the Dutch variety spoken in Flanders, northern Belgium, so it is the tongue of those Europeans.

clue.text: Intellectual, for example, finally donning cape

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
the final letter of donning
a cape is a headland, also called a head

explanation.surface: A clever person putting on a cloak, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal, slightly mocking name for a bookish highbrow person, so a noun meaning an intellectual.

clue.text: Marine creature initially placed in hold at sea

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word that follows
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first letter of placed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea animal stowed in a ship's hold during a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dolphin is a small toothed whale of the oceans, so it is an example of a sea animal.

clue.text: He may cut and run and still be caught

definitions.text: He may cut and run and still be caught

blocks.clueFragment: He may cut and run and still be caught
blocks.note: surface reading: a fugitive who slashes someone, flees and is still arrested

blocks.clueFragment: He may cut and run and still be caught
blocks.note: setter's reading: a cricketer plays a cut shot, runs between the wickets, and can be out caught

explanation.surface: A violent criminal who stabs someone and flees but is arrested anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the cut is an attacking shot square of the wicket, and a batter dismissed by a fielder catching the ball is 'caught'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer who strikes the ball, scores runs and can be dismissed by a catch is the one holding the bat.

clue.text: Suspicion about daughter's liberality

indicators.note: about means around, so the suspicion surrounds the daughter

blocks.note: a breath is a slight hint, as in a breath of scandal
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent doubting how generous their daughter really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth of mind or outlook means tolerance and openness, the sense of liberality as broad-mindedness rather than generosity.

clue.text: Inquisitive boy turned back by youth leader

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so the boy word is written from right to left
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of youth is used

blocks.note: a son is a boy child
the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A prying lad sent packing by the head of a youth club.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nosy pokes into other people's business, so the informal adjective is a synonym of prying or inquisitive.

clue.text: Either part of Royal Navy?

blocks.note: surface reading: one of the two halves of the British fleet
setter's reading: royal and navy are each a shade, and both are shades of one colour

explanation.walkthrough: Royal blue and navy blue: the colour completes both words, which is what the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a bright deep shade and navy blue a very dark one, so the colour is what either word qualifies.

clue.text: Advance my wages, back to start coaching

indicators.note: back tells us to read the request from its end to its beginning

blocks.note: to sub someone is to advance them part of their wages, so the request is SUB ME

explanation.surface: An employee asking for an advance on pay so they can begin training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaching' looks like training; here it means travelling by coach. A sub is British slang for an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To embus is to board a bus or coach, a military term for loading troops, so it is starting a coach journey.

clue.text: Spring, say, deposited in rubbish receptacle

indicators.note: something deposited in a container is put inside it

blocks.note: a bin holds rubbish
say means for example, eg

explanation.surface: A season, for example, being thrown into the dustbin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring, say' looks like a season with 'say' as the example marker; Spring is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from something is to originate or arise, so the verb means to commence or come into being.

clue.text: Unrelenting rhythm can make us exhausted

blocks.note: first meaning: the steady pulse of music
second meaning: informal for worn out

explanation.surface: A relentless pounding of music leaves us worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the regular pulse of music, and as an adjective it is informal slang for completely tired out.

clue.text: Ingenuous local missing entrance to town

indicators.note: the entrance is the way in, so the first letter of the following word is meant
missing says that letter is absent from the local word

blocks.note: a local is a native of the place
the first letter of town

explanation.surface: An unworldly villager who has never set foot in the nearby town.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive and ingenuous both describe someone innocent and trusting, lacking worldly experience, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Why not start new garden with a .shrub?

indicators.note: not starting means losing the opening letter of the question word
new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wondering why not begin a new garden with a flowering bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering garden bush with big rounded heads of blooms, so it is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Remain neutral, but delay article by criminal

blocks.note: to sit on something is to delay acting on it
the definite article
a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: A neutral party stalling a news article written by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes refusing to take sides in a dispute, staying perched between two positions, so it means staying neutral.
